# Where the v0.2 vocabularies stop fitting: evidence from 31 proposed experiments

*Generated by `outreach/build_vocab_gaps.py` on 2026-10-20. Do not hand-edit.*

This is a by-product of the SAGE experiment-design demonstration (`research/decision-sage-experiment-demo-2026-10-20.md`).
Eight open-access SAGE papers, drawn from four disciplines, each already rendered as a discourse graph. For every open
issue in those graphs a design was written, and each design had to put itself in the registry's own terms: an
`attemptType`, controls with a `kind`, and the `outcomeClass` its result would earn. The brief required a design that
could not find a fitting value to use the closest one and say so in a note, rather than force the fit silently.

That instruction turned the demonstration into a measurement. The pilot corpus is nine studies in biology and
chemistry, and the vocabularies were derived from it. These eight papers are the first time the vocabularies have been
asked to describe clinical trials, psychometrics, survey sociology, education policy, vehicle dynamics and fatigue
mechanics. They do not stretch that far.

## The measurement

| | |
|---|---|
| Designs written | 31 |
| Designs whose `attemptType` was flagged as a poor fit | 26 of 31 |
| Controls named | 104 |
| Controls whose `kind` was flagged as a poor fit | 38 of 104 |

## `attemptType`: five values, and none of them means a trial

| value | times used | of those, flagged as a poor fit |
|---|---|---|
| `wet-lab` | 11 | 7 |
| `computational` | 10 | 9 |
| `evidence-synthesis` | 1 | 1 |
| `hypothesis-generation` | 0 | 0 |
| `evaluation` | 9 | 9 |

The five values divide empirical work into wet bench, computation, synthesis of evidence, generation of hypotheses and
evaluation. Nothing in that list means a randomised clinical trial, a psychometric validation, a cohort study, a
survey, a secondary analysis of survey microdata, a fatigue test on steel, a tyre-rig measurement or a track
experiment on a vehicle. `wet-lab` became the fallback for any physical experiment, which is how a dry steel specimen
and a human drug trial both end up labelled as wet bench work. `evaluation` became the fallback for human studies that
measure people rather than materials. One design could not be labelled at all, because its fieldwork arm and its
analysis arm need different values and `attemptType` takes one: `pathType` has a `mixed` value, `attemptType` does not.

- **bicycle** (iss-2), used `computational`: The first block is a re-analysis of someone else's published bench measurements, so it sits between computational and evidence-synthesis; if new rig measurements are added it becomes a physical bench experiment, for which the vocabulary offers only wet-lab.
- **bicycle** (iss-3), used `wet-lab`: This is a bench measurement campaign on a tyre test rig followed by a simulation re-run. It is a physical experiment but nothing about it is wet or biological; wet-lab is simply the only physical-experiment value the vocabulary offers, and the honest label would be bench-measurement plus computational.
- **bicycle** (iss-4), used `wet-lab`: This is a physical track experiment on a vehicle, paired with pre-registered simulation predictions. Neither wet-lab nor computational describes it; the vocabulary has no value for a field or track experiment and no value for a mixed physical and computational attempt.
- **camouflaging** (iss-1), used `evaluation`: This is a psychometric validation study in human participants. 'Evaluation' is the nearest value because what is under test is the behaviour of measurement instruments rather than a biological hypothesis, but none of the five values covers psychometrics.
- **camouflaging** (iss-2), used `evaluation`: This is a prospective observational cohort with repeated measures in human participants. None of the five values covers a longitudinal human study, and 'wet-lab' or 'computational' would be plainly wrong, so 'evaluation' is used as the least misleading.
- **camouflaging** (iss-3), used `evaluation`: A cross-sectional comparative study in human participants with blinded behavioural coding. 'Evaluation' is the nearest of the five values; none describes a group-comparison study with an equivalence test as its primary analysis.
- **camouflaging** (iss-4), used `evaluation`: An accelerated longitudinal cohort study in children and young people. As with the other designs, none of the five values describes a human developmental cohort, and 'evaluation' is used as the least misleading.
- **gbcs** (iss-1), used `computational`: This is secondary statistical analysis of existing social-survey microdata. The NRR value 'computational' is shaped for simulation, modelling and machine-learning work; 'evidence-synthesis' is wrong because no published effect estimates are being pooled. 'computational' is the closest of the five but describes the tooling, not the kind of inquiry.
- **gbcs** (iss-2), used `computational`: This is a re-specification of a latent variable model on survey microdata. 'computational' is the closest of the five NRR values but implies simulation or machine learning rather than secondary survey analysis; none of the five has a value for re-estimating a published statistical model under an alternative measurement.
- **gbcs** (iss-3), used `evaluation`: In NRR 'evaluation' means scoring a model or agent against a benchmark task. Here what is scored is three survey estimators against a probability-sample benchmark, which is the same shape of activity on a different kind of object. 'computational' was the runner-up and describes the tooling, but 'evaluation' describes what the experiment is for.
- **gbcs** (iss-4), used `computational`: A poor fit, and worth recording. Arm A is secondary data linkage and benchmarking, for which 'computational' is the closest value. Arm B is primary qualitative fieldwork plus blinded human coding, for which the vocabulary has no value at all: the only primary-data-collection value is 'wet-lab', which is plainly wrong, and 'evidence-synthesis' does not cover collecting new data. A mixed-methods design cannot be labelled correctly with one value from this list.
- **kindergarten** (iss-1), used `computational`: This is a secondary statistical analysis of national survey and child assessment microdata. In the NRR vocabulary 'computational' means simulation or in-silico work, and there is no value for observational analysis of an existing cohort, which is what this is.
- **kindergarten** (iss-2), used `computational`: This is a quasi-experimental policy evaluation on survey microdata with hand-coded policy histories. 'computational' is the closest of the five values but means simulation or in-silico work; the vocabulary has no value for observational policy evaluation.
- **kindergarten** (iss-3), used `evaluation`: This is primary survey measurement work: a questionnaire-wording calibration with daily teacher logs and independent classroom observation. In the NRR vocabulary 'evaluation' means benchmarking a model or system, and there is no value for instrument calibration or for primary field measurement in a school.
- **kindergarten** (iss-4), used `computational`: This is a pre-registered reanalysis of an existing dataset under several model specifications. The vocabulary has no value for reanalysis, robustness replication or a multiverse analysis, and 'computational' here means only that the work happens in a statistics package.
- **psilocybin** (iss-1), used `wet-lab`: This is a human pharmacodynamic dose-ranging study. None of the five permitted attemptType values describes a clinical drug administration study in people; wet-lab is the closest because the work is empirical measurement on human subjects rather than computation or synthesis.
- **psilocybin** (iss-2), used `wet-lab`: Again a human randomised clinical trial with an embedded measure-validation sub-study. The five permitted values have no entry for a clinical trial or for psychometric validation, so wet-lab is used as the closest fit for empirical work on human subjects.
- **psilocybin** (iss-3), used `wet-lab`: A multisite human randomised trial. No permitted attemptType value covers a clinical trial, so wet-lab is used for the same reason as in the other designs.
- **psilocybin** (iss-4), used `wet-lab`: A longitudinal human neuroimaging study nested in a clinical trial. It is neither wet bench work nor computation nor synthesis; wet-lab is the closest permitted value for empirical measurement on human subjects, and the misfit is worth recording.
- **tenere** (iss-1), used `evaluation`: None of the five values names a randomised controlled trial in human patients. 'evaluation' is the closest because the object is an intervention being judged against a comparator, but the graph JSON itself uses the free-text value 'randomized trial' for the same thing.
- **tenere** (iss-2), used `computational`: This is a secondary analysis of individual patient data from a completed trial, together with a power simulation. 'computational' is the closest of the five; none of them names a re-analysis of trial data.
- **tenere** (iss-3), used `evaluation`: This is a randomised methodological study nested inside a clinical trial, a study-within-a-trial. 'evaluation' is the closest of the five values, but what is being evaluated is a trial design feature, not a treatment.
- **tenere** (iss-4), used `evaluation`: This is a randomised management-strategy trial triggered by a laboratory event and embedded in a disease registry. 'evaluation' is the closest; none of the five values names a strategy trial, and 'wet-lab' would be plainly wrong for a clinical blood test.
- **welded** (iss-1), used `wet-lab`: None of the five values covers a mechanical fatigue test on metal. I used wet-lab because it is the only value that means a physical bench experiment, but nothing in this design is wet, biological or chemical. The field needs a value such as mechanical-test or bench-experiment.
- **welded** (iss-2), used `computational`: This is one study with two halves, a literature compilation and a regression on the compiled data, which map to evidence-synthesis and computational respectively. The vocabulary forces a single value. The schema's pathType has a mixed value but attemptType does not, so the mixture is lost.
- **welded** (iss-3), used `evidence-synthesis`: The corpus arm is evidence synthesis, but this design also has a prospective bench arm in which new specimens are cut with the notch at different distances from the weld centreline. No single value covers a study with both a synthesis arm and a laboratory arm, and splitting it into two attempts would break the shared pre-registered decision rule that makes it a test rather than two descriptions.

## Control kinds: shaped for the bench

| value | times used | of those, flagged as a poor fit |
|---|---|---|
| `adversarial-label` | 7 | 3 |
| `background` | 13 | 9 |
| `designated` | 25 | 8 |
| `internal-positive` | 12 | 0 |
| `isotype` | 1 | 0 |
| `known-positive-task` | 11 | 6 |
| `no-treatment` | 8 | 4 |
| `none` | 1 | 1 |
| `vehicle` | 7 | 4 |
| `within-subject` | 19 | 3 |

The ten kinds come from cell and animal work. What these fields actually control for has no entry: an active placebo,
an attention- or arousal-matched comparator arm, an active comparator drug, a littermate genetic-background control, a
non-targeting construct, a blinding check, a permutation null, a specification baseline, an instrument noise floor, a
cross-rig calibration repeat, and the known-answer reference case that engineering leans on hardest. `designated`
absorbed the most traffic precisely because it is the vaguest value available.

- **bicycle** (iss-1), used `known-positive-task`: In this field the known-positive task is a published parameter set with published eigenvalues, not a positive control reagent.
- **bicycle** (iss-1), used `background`: Used here as a numerical noise floor, not a biological background signal.
- **bicycle** (iss-2), used `known-positive-task`: Again a published numeric result standing in for a positive control.
- **bicycle** (iss-2), used `no-treatment`: Here no-treatment means a manoeuvre with no drive or brake torque, not an untreated subject.
- **bicycle** (iss-3), used `background`: Used as an instrument repeatability and drift floor, not a background signal.
- **bicycle** (iss-3), used `designated`: In this field the designated control is a cross-instrument calibration repeat, not a designated positive control sample.
- **bicycle** (iss-4), used `known-positive-task`: A published measurement standing in for a positive control.
- **bicycle** (iss-4), used `background`: A sensor noise floor and structural resonance check rather than a biological background.
- **bicycle** (iss-4), used `designated`: A reference specimen bracketing the model idealisation, not a designated positive sample.
- **gbcs** (iss-1), used `known-positive-task`: In NRR this value means a benchmark task with a known-good answer. Here it is a predictor with a published positive effect used the same way: if it fails to recover, the pipeline is broken rather than the hypothesis refuted.
- **gbcs** (iss-1), used `designated`: Used here as an age placebo rather than as a designated positive control sample.
- **gbcs** (iss-2), used `within-subject`: The unit held constant is the couple rather than the person, which the vocabulary does not distinguish.
- **gbcs** (iss-2), used `designated`: Used as a null-case sample rather than a designated positive sample.
- **gbcs** (iss-2), used `no-treatment`: There is no treatment to withhold. This records that the design has no intervention arm, which is why a conventional negative control cannot be specified. The honest statement is that the baseline is the paper's own published household specification.
- **gbcs** (iss-3), used `adversarial-label`: In NRR this means a deliberately wrong label in a machine-learning sense. Here it is a pre-registered permutation null: occupational categories are shuffled across web-survey respondents.
- **gbcs** (iss-4), used `adversarial-label`: A blinding check rather than a corrupted training label.
- **kindergarten** (iss-1), used `known-positive-task`: The vocabulary means a benchmark task a model is known to pass. Here the positive control is a published association that the analysis pipeline must recover from the same pooled data before any null elsewhere is believed.
- **kindergarten** (iss-1), used `background`: This is a placebo-outcome falsification test. The NRR negative-control kinds are written for treated and untreated biological samples and have no value for a pre-exposure outcome regressed on later exposure.
- **kindergarten** (iss-2), used `no-treatment`: The vocabulary means an untreated biological sample. Here it is a population not exposed to the policy, which is the same logic but a different object.
- **kindergarten** (iss-2), used `designated`: Used here as a falsification outcome rather than a known-good sample, which the vocabulary does not provide for.
- **kindergarten** (iss-2), used `background`: Used for a parallel-trends check, which has no NRR control kind.
- **kindergarten** (iss-3), used `designated`: These are anchor items in the equating sense. The NRR control kinds have no value for an anchor item whose measurement is assumed stable.
- **kindergarten** (iss-3), used `background`: An external measurement comparator rather than a background signal level.
- **kindergarten** (iss-4), used `designated`: A replication target standing in for a known-good reference sample, which the vocabulary does not provide for.
- **kindergarten** (iss-4), used `background`: A worst-case bound rather than a background measurement.
- **microglia** (iss-1), used `vehicle`: A sequence-matched non-targeting adeno-associated virus is only loosely a vehicle in the sense the vocabulary intends; it is the same delivery vector with inert cargo.
- **microglia** (iss-3), used `within-subject`: Applies only to the multi-electrode array arm, where each well is recorded before and after medium transfer.
- **microglia** (iss-4), used `background`: A littermate wild type genotype is a genetic background control, which the vocabulary has no dedicated kind for; background is the closest and is being used here for strain background rather than for assay background signal.
- **psilocybin** (iss-1), used `vehicle`: The inert capsule is a true placebo rather than a pharmacological vehicle for a dissolved agent, but vehicle is the closest available kind.
- **psilocybin** (iss-2), used `vehicle`: The comparator is an active placebo chosen to mimic somatic sensation, not an inert pharmacological vehicle, so vehicle is an imperfect fit.
- **psilocybin** (iss-3), used `vehicle`: An active placebo rather than a pharmacological vehicle.
- **tenere** (iss-1), used `known-positive-task`: In a clinical trial this is an assay-sensitivity control, not a task. The closest listed kind is known-positive-task because the point is a measure already shown to move.
- **tenere** (iss-3), used `adversarial-label`: The listed kind fits: participants are asked to guess the label, and better-than-chance guessing invalidates the manipulation.
- **welded** (iss-1), used `designated`: designated is the closest value, but in the vocabulary it means a designated positive control sample in an assay. Here the designated reference is a specimen condition, not a reagent or a known-active sample.
- **welded** (iss-1), used `no-treatment`: no-treatment maps onto no stress relief and no closure correction only loosely. There is no treatment in the biological sense, only a specimen left in the condition the 2016 paper tested.
- **welded** (iss-1), used `within-subject`: A constant-amplitude fatigue test cannot carry two load amplitudes in one specimen, so this is a within-specimen comparison across crack length rather than across the condition being varied.
- **welded** (iss-2), used `none`: There is no positive control in the assay sense available here, because no joint has a published, independently established set of true coefficients to recover. The known-positive-task entry above is the nearest substitute and it only checks the pipeline, not the quantity of interest.
- **welded** (iss-3), used `background`: background in the vocabulary means an assay background signal. Here it is a material condition where the effect is expected to be absent, which is the same logic but not the same thing.

## What to do about it

Three options, in increasing order of commitment.

1. **Leave the vocabularies alone and keep the notes.** The `*Note` fields already carry the truth, and the pages
   print them. Cheapest, and it leaves every cross-field query wrong: a search for `wet-lab` returns a steel fatigue
   test and a psilocybin trial.
2. **Add the missing values.** For `attemptType`: a value for a trial or prospective human study, one for a physical
   bench or field measurement that is not wet work, one for secondary analysis of existing data, and a `mixed` value
   as `pathType` already has. For control kinds: `active-comparator`, `active-placebo`, `genetic-background`,
   `non-targeting-construct`, `blinding-check`, `permutation-null`, `reference-case`, `instrument-noise-floor`.
   This is a schema change and the convergence test would have to be rerun.
3. **Make the controls vocabulary extensible per profile**, the way the biology profile already specialises other
   fields, so a field can declare its own control kinds against a small shared core. Most work, and the only option
   that survives the next discipline.

The decision is not made here. What is established here is that the gap is real, that it appears in 26 of
31 designs rather than in one awkward case, and that it is concentrated in exactly the places a federation of
nodes beyond biology would first be asked to serve.

## Note on the evidence

These are machine-written designs, not published studies, so the misfits are reports of what a design could not say
cleanly rather than observed failures of a real deposit. The value is that each one names the field, the value it was
forced to use, and what the field actually needed. Every design is in `outreach/sage-experiments/<paper>.json` and is
checked by `outreach/check_sage_experiments.py`, which also prints this evidence with `--gaps`.

## Decision, 2026-10-21

Option 2 was taken. Fourteen vocabulary terms were added in schema v0.2.5 (`../schema/CHANGELOG.md`): five attempt
types (`clinical-trial`, `observational-study`, `bench-measurement`, `secondary-analysis`, `mixed`), two positive
control kinds (`active-comparator`, `reference-case`) and seven negative control kinds (`placebo`, `active-placebo`,
`genetic-background`, `non-targeting-construct`, `permutation-null`, `instrument-noise-floor`, `blinding-check`).
Nothing structural changed and no existing record uses any of them, so the corpus is unchanged.

The release records them as forced by proposals rather than by deposits, which is a weaker kind of evidence than the
nine encoded studies and is stated as such. Option 3, per-profile extensible control kinds, remains open; fourteen
terms in one release is the argument for it.

The designs written against the six NEJM papers on 2026-10-21 are the first use of the new terms, and the misfit notes
they produce are the test of whether these fourteen were named correctly.
